localBiteReport: The most recent full report covering Choctawhatchee Bay and the Destin area (Great Days Outdoors, week of Oct 30–Nov 5, 2026) puts redfish as the top inshore target heading into November, with schools stacking around bridges, jetties, and the East Pass; fish in good numbers and quality pompano still mixed in. Speckled trout are also showing up in the 22- to 27-inch range wherever bait concentrations can be located, though an unsettled fall transition — recent hurricane impacts, warm spells, and short-lived fronts — has left both redfish and trout scattered between their late-summer and winter haunts. A separate report from the prior week (Oct 23–29) by Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters noted that Choctawhatchee Bay avoided heavy mudding after the storm, staying clear enough for sight fishing redfish on the flats, with fish under about 23 inches still holding in guts and potholes; cut mullet on Carolina rigs was the standout bait. Water temperature for this area is 75°F as of today's reading. The Half Hitch Destin tackle shop posted its most recent report on 10-26-26, though full body content was not accessible; the flounder run window (typically mid-Oct through mid-Nov) is likely in its tail-end phase based on seasonal timing.
